subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Stingray Phone Trackers
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Stingray Phone Trackers.

hook.text: A device that pretends to be a cell tower, tricking every phone nearby into connecting to it.

buildup.text: Stingrays — also called IMSI catchers — intercept calls, texts, and location data from phones.

discovery.text: Police use Stingrays to track suspects. But they also capture data from everyone nearby.

twist.text: Law enforcement was so secretive about Stingrays that prosecutors dropped cases to avoid revealing them.

climax.text: A surveillance tool so powerful that police would rather lose a case than admit they used it.

punchline.text: Track one suspect. Capture a whole neighborhood.

quiz.question: How does a Stingray surveillance device work?
options: It mimics a cell tower to trick phones into connecting
It hacks into phone operating systems remotely
